allVisibleCapturedMeaning: true = every quest VISIBLE to this profile was captured, completed, active, failed, or listed-but-locked, across every tab the trader shows. It does NOT mean every quest the trader has: anything still gated behind an unfinished quest or an unreached loyalty level is not on screen and is therefore not here. No trader in this collection is complete in the absolute sense.
allVisibleCapturedNote: Every Prapor tab is covered: LL1-LL4 plus the essential group.

profile.note: Confirmed PvE on 2026-08-10, and corroborated by the Fence batch, whose '[PVE ZONE]' cards carry ids that exist only in tarkov.dev's pve task list. Earlier batches were recorded as unconfirmed rather than guessed. It changes nothing in the comparisons, the three modes are identical on every field across the 483 quests they share, but provenance should say what is known.
profile.factionNote: USEC. DETERMINED FROM THE COLLECTION ITSELF, not something written down at capture time. Four quests are faction-exclusive with no counterpart id: Road Closed (USEC), Green Corridor (BEAR), Our Own Land (BEAR) and Counteraction (USEC). "Road Closed" is ACTIVE on this profile, and the wiki says outright that it is "only obtainable by USEC PMCs" with Green Corridor as its BEAR counterpart. Both BEAR-only quests are absent from Prapor's list, which was captured in full. A BEAR profile could not show Road Closed and would have to show the other two, so the reading is unambiguous.

reading: Read off the in-game quest screen. `location` is the single map the game prints in the header, which is NOT the union of the objective maps and is not always consistent with them (see Debut vs Shootout Picnic). Objective text is verbatim, including the (Optional) prefix. `availableAtLoyalty` is the loyalty tab the quest was listed under, the roman numeral in the top-right of the quest card.
categoryMeaning: The trader's quests are not all filed under a loyalty level. Prapor also has an ESSENTIAL group, marked with a list glyph instead of a roman numeral, holding the numbered story lines (The Punisher, Hell on Earth, The Good Times, Shipping Delay) plus Big Customer. Those records carry `category` and NO `availableAtLoyalty`, the two are alternatives, and inventing a loyalty level for them would put false rows in the chain-break table.
statusValues: completed | active | failed. `failed` is real and observed (Big Customer), a quest can be permanently failed and still sit in the list.
objectivesCompleteMeaning: false = the screenshot was cut off before the end of the objective list, so the COUNT is a lower bound and must not be graded. Every record here is true: I confirmed the cards were captured whole, including the ones whose last row sits at the image edge. Set it to false only when a capture is KNOWN to be partial.

quests.name: Glory to CPSU
quests.questIdReason: CORRECTED. The wiki DOES title this id's page 'Glory to CPSU', matching the game exactly, but our fetcher had cached it as 'Glory to CPSU - Part 1' because its move-chain follower ran to the end of a chain and landed on the wrong page (the same bug that filed a SKILL page under Jaeger's 'First Aid'). With the chain fix the wiki title now corroborates this pin independently. The pin is kept because it is still ambiguous by NAME: every source publishes two quests, 'Glory to CPSU - Part 1' (639135b04ed9512be67647d7) and '- Part 2' (64f5aac4b63b74469b6c14c2), and the observed name is a substring of both. Pinned to Part 2 because the observed first objective is Part 2's first objective verbatim, while Part 1's only real objective now appears here as an (Optional) line. The reading is that 1.1.0 MERGED the two into one quest named 'Glory to CPSU', the same pattern later confirmed by content for Easy Job, The Bunker and Pets Won't Need It. Corroborated three ways: the wiki redirects its Part 2 page to the Part 1 page, so its editors merged them too; and 'Glory to CPSU - Part 1' is one of the 22 Prapor quests tarkov.dev publishes that are absent from my own complete list, exactly as an absorbed half should be.
